episode.tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
episode.title: What Are AI Skills, Tools, and Memory?
episode.disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario. Wouri Express and its people are invented; the setting draws on documented conditions in Douala, Cameroon.

onScreen.text: The Delay Analyst forgot everything it learned last week.
onScreen.emphasis: A model alone has no hands and no memory. You add both.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Last week the Delay Analyst learned that checkpoint delays count as road delays. This week it asked Ndedi the same question again.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A model on its own has no hands and no memory. Skills, tools and memory give it both. Here is what each one is.

onScreen.title: What Are AI Skills, Tools, and Memory?
onScreen.subtitle: AI Fundamentals · Lesson 7 · Equipping the Delay Analyst at Wouri Express, Douala

items.text: It asked about checkpoints again: no memory
It sorted a message wrongly: no procedure for that case
It could not check the distance to Edéa: no tool

messages.text: Mbella: Whatever it remembers must be something I can open and read. No black box.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Ndedi has three complaints, Tanyi. It forgot the checkpoint decision, sorted one message wrongly, and could not check the distance to Edéa.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Three complaints, three missing parts: memory, a skill, a tool. And Mbella's condition: whatever it remembers, she can open and read.

onScreen.title: Skills, tools and memory around one model

nodes.label: Skills
nodes.sub: written procedures: how to do a task

nodes.label: Tools
nodes.sub: things it can call: sheet, map, messages

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A skill is a written procedure. How to sort a delay. How to write the report. The model follows it like a junior reading a checklist.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A tool is something the model can call: read the sheet, measure a distance, export messages. Its hands into your systems.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Memory is what it keeps between runs: decisions, findings, preferences. Plain files the company can open.

left.title: Put it in a skill
items: Anything Ndedi would write in a procedure

right.title: Put it in memory
items: “Week 36: port queues were the top cause”

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: What goes where? Rules Ndedi would write in a procedure go in a skill. Things learned while working go in memory.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Checkpoint counts as road is a rule. Week thirty-six's top cause is a finding. Mbella prefers short reports is a preference.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: And memory has a rule of its own. No customer names, no phone numbers. Findings, not people.

items.text: Read the message. Pick one cause: port, road, customer, other
No cause in the text: not stated. Never guess
Week 36: top cause port queues, 9:00 slot
Ndedi decided: checkpoints file under road

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: First, a skill: a short text file on how to sort a delay, with Ndedi's cases. Checkpoint means road. No cause means not stated.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Then a new tool, map distance, to check how far Edéa really is. And memory is just a notes file?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: A notes file I read at the start of every run and add to at the end. Mbella can open it. No black box.

messages.text: Port queues at 9:00, as always. Memory says so.

ui.title: Check
lines: This week's messages: no port queue mentioned
Ndedi: port gate now opens at 7:00

items.text: Fresh data beats an old note
Ndedi reviews the notes file monthly

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Delivery fourteen? Port queues at nine, as always. It is in the memory, so it must be true.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: That note is from week thirty-six. This week's messages mention no port queue, and Ndedi says the gate now opens at seven. Outdated.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Memory helps until it goes stale. So every note carries a date, fresh data beats an old note, and Ndedi reviews the file monthly.

steps.title: Skill, tool and memory at work

messages.text: Week 38 report ready. Checkpoints filed under road (your decision, week 37). Edéa run: 62 km by road, first delivery, no history.

ui.title: Update memory: port gate opens at 7:00 from week 38?
summary: Old note kept with its date

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Friday: checkpoints filed under road from memory, the Edéa distance from the map tool, and no repeated questions.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: A new note about the port hours goes in only when Ndedi confirms it. Memory is written with a person watching.

onScreen.title: Skill, tool, memory in other jobs

items.label: Support desk
items.text: Skill: refund procedure. Tool: order lookup. Memory: open cases

items.label: Clinic
items.text: Skill: triage checklist. Tool: appointment book. Memory: follow-ups due

items.label: Recruiting
items.text: Skill: screening criteria. Tool: applications inbox. Memory: roles already filled

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: In a support desk: the refund procedure is a skill, order lookup a tool, open cases the memory. A clinic and a recruiter split the same way.

onScreen.title: Who owns this?
items: Skills are written by Ndedi, in files the company keeps
Tools reach only the company's own systems
Memory holds findings and decisions, never people's data
Accountable: the person who reviews the notes

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Skills are Ndedi's files. Tools reach only the company's systems. Memory holds findings and decisions, never people's data. The reviewer is accountable.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Skills say how. Tools give hands. Memory keeps what was learned. Around one model, in files you can open.

onScreen.title: Your build challenge
items: Write one skill as a half-page procedure
Write what it should remember, with dates

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Your challenge: write one skill as a half-page procedure. Then list the tools it needs and what it should remember.

tanyi.name: Tanyi
tanyi.role: AI engineer and instructor, the animated host. Middle-aged Black African man. Calm, direct, practical. Has built and operated real systems.

amara.name: Amara
amara.role: Curious learner who asks the questions beginners are thinking.

kito.name: Kito
kito.role: Small AI assistant who demonstrates concepts and occasionally makes believable mistakes.

hallucinator.name: The Hallucinator
hallucinator.role: Mischievous. Represents confident but incorrect AI output.

gatekeeper.name: The Gatekeeper
gatekeeper.role: Represents security, privacy, governance and human approval.
